customer_attendees: Dr. Elena Voss - Head of ML
next_steps: Redwood to upload per-run CSV of latency/throughput with config tags to shared drive by 2028-04-13
Helixoria to confirm peak QPS and 95th percentile latency target by 2028-04-14
Schedule on-prem smoke test window (2 hours) with Carmen and Jared week of 2028-04-17
action_items: Maya: share annotated benchmark CSV + notes (due 2028-04-13)
Jared: run targeted 95th-percentile tail noise tests with KV-cache disabled and share logs (due 2028-04-14)

summary: Weekly pilot check-in focusing on benchmark deltas vs the incumbent. Redwood presented tuned runs where continuous batching and prefix caching reduced token latency at 95th percentile by ~18% in the mid-load window but saw burst tail spikes under cold KV cache. Action items agreed for targeted tail testing, CSV delivery, and an on-prem smoke window.
topics: continuous batching and batch size tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-04-11 14:00 UTC | Duration ~42m | Redwood: Maya, Jared, Sofia, Tom | Helixoria: Elena, Ravi, Carmen, Marcus

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off - this is the week three pilot lab sprint review, quick who we have?
[00:07] Ravi Menon: ravi here, elena and carmen and marcus with me - thanks for organizing.
[00:12] Maya Chen: great. Jared will take the bench walkthrough, i'll cover next steps and pricing bits at the end.
[00:18] Jared Patel: cool hi all, quick agenda - show the baseline+redwood runs, config diffs, tail noise triage, suggestions for routing and private smoke tests.
[00:28] [00:30] Jared Patel: so first slide, mid-load steady state at 500 qps, payloads are average 120 tokens - incumbent 95th pctl was 420ms, our tuned hosted run 95th pctl 345ms so about 18% improvement, median almost same. note: we used prefix caching and continuous batching at target batch size 8.
[01:05] Dr. Elena Voss: hmm that's promising, did you change the sequence lengths or quantization for that run?
[01:12] Jared Patel: good question, we kept FP16 kernels, no quantization for that run - we did one quantized run Q4 int8 style and saw 12% slower tail but lower unit cost — tradeoff there.
[01:25] Carmen Ortiz: can you clarify "KV cash" — sorry i mean KV cache — when does that come into play? we saw a few spikes in our logs when we restarted the worker.
[01:33] Jared Patel: yes cold KV cache is about warmup - initial requests hit full compute path and you see tail spikes. our fix is to pre-warm prefixes and keep a small dedup cache on the router. we also saw that the incumbent has a longer warmup window because of their batching policy.
[01:52] [02:00] Marcus Lee: in the spike sample at 1am you had an outlier 1.2s 95th - what's causing that? network or infer?
[02:07] Tom Becker: we dug into traces, most of those were backend KV misses plus a transient routing retry. there's also a small chunk from inter-zone network variance - remember this was on hosted cross-region.
[02:22] Dr. Elena Voss: network variance matters because we plan to run in our VPC eventually. if we go private does that remove inter-zone jitter?
[02:30] Sofia Ruiz: usually private/VPC reduces multi-tenant noisy neighbor network variance but you still need to pin regions and keep latency SLOs at the infra layer. also KMS calls for key access introduce subtle latency on cold starts, we can show configs to mitigate.
[02:48] [03:00] Jared Patel: moving on - throughput sustained runs: under 800 qps we maintained 98% success and linear scaling on dedicated slots; the incumbent dropped throughput by ~12% at the same load with higher cost. Our unit cost per 1k tokens was 14% lower for the mid-load profiles.
[03:25] Ravi Menon: that's good, cost is meaningful — can you share the config for autoscale thresholds?
[03:31] Jared Patel: yes it's in the CSV. short version: scale at 70% GPU util, max burst of two slots, cooldown 45s. That cooldown is tuned down from default 90s which helped tail but increased cost slightly.
[03:48] [04:00] Dr. Elena Voss: what about model fallbacks? if a slot is saturated do you route to a cheaper quantized variant? we need graceful degradation.
[04:09] Jared Patel: absolutely - we have router policies: prefer full-fp model for low latency, fallback to quantized variant when queue depth > threshold. We can make fallback thresholds more conservative for you.
[04:26] Marcus Lee: any effect on hallucination rates when falling back to quantized?
[04:31] Tom Becker: we ran automated evals on a golden prompt set; small increase in token-level perplexity but for your reranking scenario the pass-through metrics stayed within acceptable bounds; we'll include the eval CSV.
[04:50] [05:00] Carmen Ortiz: security: SOC2, SSO, KMS - we need specifics for the private pilot. last time we saw docs but not network diagrams.
[05:09] Maya Chen: noted - we'll attach the SOC2 report and an architecture diagram for the VPC private deployment; KMS integrations include AWS KMS and HSM options, and SAML/SSO provisioning via Okta.
[05:22] Dr. Elena Voss: audit logs granularity? we want token-level attribution for compliance.
[05:28] Sofia Ruiz: we can stream audit logs to your SIEM, include request/response IDs (not full PII by default), and we support longer retention for enterprise add-on.
[05:42] [06:00] Jared Patel: back to bench - we identified two main tail causes: cold KV cache and retry backoff on transient GPU OOMs when batch size spikes. For the latter we added a soft cap on batch size and proactive queuing.
[06:19] Ravi Menon: GPU OOMs — are those because of mixed sequence lengths at scale?
[06:24] Jared Patel: yes mixing long tails with short prompts causes packing inefficiency and occasional OOMs under heavy batching; our packing heuristic now is length-aware and we overflow to a safe lane.
[06:36] [07:00] Dr. Elena Voss: can you quantify the reduction in OOM events?
[07:04] Jared Patel: reduced by roughly 87% in our stress runs after the packing fix, measured over 10k requests.
[07:12] Marcus Lee: nice. on the runs you showed, what was the hardware spec? GPU type?
[07:17] Tom Becker: these were A100 equivalents in hosted, dedicated clusters tested on v4 ext types for parity; for private we can run on your on-prem nodes or recommend 80GB class GPUs.
[07:32] [08:00] Carmen Ortiz: for the private pilot, we'll need a small on-prem smoke test to validate cold-starts - can you scope 2 hours with your SE?
[08:07] Maya Chen: yes we'll do a smoke window with Jared and Tom — Carmen can pick a day next week.
[08:15] Dr. Elena Voss: earlier you mentioned quantized runs had slower tail but lower unit cost - can you share cost delta?
[08:22] Jared Patel: quantized int8 runs reduced unit compute cost approx 26% but tail 95th rose 10-15% depending on prompt mix; for reranking where response fidelity is important we recommend staged fallback with eval gating.
[08:41] [09:00] Marcus Lee: is there a clear recommendation to hit our 95th target of <400ms under 600qps?
[09:07] Jared Patel: our recommendation path: hosted tuned FP16 with prefix pre-warm + capped batch size; if you need cost lower, use quantized with stricter routing and golden-set eval gating. For private pilot we can likely hit <400ms at 600qps but we need the on-prem smoke to confirm network/KMS effects.
[09:33] Ravi Menon: what about reranking latency — we run a 3-pass reranker, the total endpoint has to be <650ms. How should we pipeline?
[09:41] Tom Becker: pipeline recommendation: do a short-list generation on full model then rerank with a leaner variant, or use our async rerank route that streams partial results — cuts end-to-end by around 120-180ms in tests.
[10:00] [10:30] Dr. Elena Voss: any concerns about model degradation when splitting gen vs rerank?
[10:35] Jared Patel: slight mismatch risk, but you can lock the re-ranker to same tokenizer and seed behavior, plus we run evals to catch regressions.
[10:50] Marcus Lee: okay can you give an example run config we should replicate locally?
[10:55] Jared Patel: i'll put full run configs in the shared CSV - includes batch size, pack heuristics, prefix cache policy, kv pre-warming steps.
[11:10] [12:00] Carmen Ortiz: firewall and private network question — we use strict egress, will Redwood need open egress to KMS endpoints?
[12:09] Sofia Ruiz: for managed KMS you'll need KMS egress; for full air-gapped on-prem we offer HSM connector that doesn't require outbound. We'll document both options.
[12:27] Dr. Elena Voss: also compliance — can we redact logs for PII in test runs?
[12:33] Sofia Ruiz: yes we can configure redaction and log sampling; we'll propose defaults and you can opt-in for full capture for debugging.
[12:46] [13:00] Maya Chen: quick commercial note — if you go dedicated or private the committed capacity pricing differs and we can bake in discount tiers tied to committed slots. i'll send preliminary numbers.
[13:14] Ravi Menon: we need a 3-month cost estimate for projected 400-800 qps.
[13:20] Maya Chen: noted, will include conservative and optimistic columns.
[13:28] [14:00] Jared Patel: technical triage plan: run isolated tail tests with KV disabled to measure baseline compute-only tail, run with KV pre-warm to see delta, and run inter-zone network emulation to reproduce jitter. we recommend one focused 2-hour smoke session for private pilot.
[14:47] Dr. Elena Voss: sounds good. timelines?
[14:51] Maya Chen: i'll post CSV and run logs by Thursday (2028-04-13). Jared will run the tail tests by Friday (2028-04-14). Carmen to open firewall ticket and propose two 2-hour windows by Monday.
[15:08] Marcus Lee: perfect. anything else?
[15:12] Tom Becker: i'll attach the eval pass rates and hallucination metrics.
[15:18] [16:00] Dr. Elena Voss: thanks all, this is helpful. Rapid question — do you recommend changing our prompt templates to reduce long tails?
[16:25] Jared Patel: yes truncation and canonicalization help a lot; we can share a short doc with best-practices.
[16:33] Maya Chen: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[16:40] [17:00] -- Recap --
[17:05] Maya Chen: Action items: share CSV + annotated notes (Maya), run tail tests (Jared), open firewall ticket (Carmen), provide prompt set (Elena). Schedule smoke window (Carmen/Jared). Pricing estimate (Maya).
[17:30] Ravi Menon: thanks, we'll look for the CSV and pick a smoke day.
[17:35] Dr. Elena Voss: thanks everyone.
[17:40] Maya Chen: thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
